correctness.rationale: The recursively sorted rooted-forest generator enumerates each isomorphism class of trivially perfect graph exactly once, by recursive universal-vertex decomposition. Direct adjacency construction is exact. Exhaustive enumeration through n=9 (1204 total types) confirms the maxima and one extremizer in the order-8 general and order-9 connected classes. Two independent implementations of iterative stable color partitions agree on every instance, all generated graphs were tested P4/C4-free, and the star/paw witness admits a direct three-split argument. Thus both existence and minimality/uniqueness hold without extrapolating finite samples to infinite claims.

value.rationale: The strict splitting round count is a natural complexity/logic-depth invariant of color refinement. The exact first thresholds n=8 and n=9 (connected), with unique extremizing structures and complete class-specific small-order profiles, are an intrinsically motivated natural cutoff rather than a hand-picked graph. It calibrates the first emergence of delayed information propagation in a broad hereditary class and provides sharp finite base cases for further iteration analysis.
